description: Hey, I’m Roi and I will use this podcast to help me expand on the my healing journey experiences.

title: Where to start?
description: So I had a choice to make. Hundreds of threads to pull, and yet I knew each one would tighten the knot on another.

title: The Healing Power of Empathy in Medicine
description: Empathy in medicine is trainable, and it's measurably declining across medical education. What the research says about why, and what's actually shown to reverse it.

title: The Way Out
description: It's a harsh realization: you pull through life with chronic illness, trying to survive day by day, but you are not living.

title: Health IT is broken, Let's fix it.
description: Nurses buried in data entry, doctors transcribing instead of treating, patients repeating their history at every login. Health IT doesn't need another app. It needs one shared standard.

title: A Tapestry of Strength: Fostering Collaboration in Patient Advocacy
description: Patient advocacy groups mostly compete for the same limited attention and funding. They'd do more for patients by sharing infrastructure than by competing for it.

title: Every Chronic Illness Has a Mental Health Component
description: The physical symptoms get all the attention: the pain, the fatigue, the appointments. Having lived with chronic illness for years, the mental toll is just as real, and it's almost never treated as part of the same condition.

title: Case managers: The missing link of Healthcare
description: Doctors diagnose the problem. Case managers are the ones who actually navigate the system around it. Why that role does more for patient empowerment than most of what claims to.

title: Invisible Champions: Why Supporting Caregivers Strengthens Us All
description: Caregivers manage the medications, the appointments, and the daily reality of a chronic condition, and healthcare mostly treats them as support staff instead of the experts they've become.

title: Lost in the Labyrinth: Why Health Literacy is the Key to Patient Empowerment
description: Health knowledge sits locked away in academic language most patients were never taught to read. That's not a patient failing. It's a design failure.

title: The Duality of Illness: Embracing the Journey While Demanding Recognition
description: Chronic illness demands two contradictory things at once: acknowledge how real it is, and refuse to be defined only by it. Both, at the same time, all the time.

title: The Bias Silencing Women in Healthcare
description: Women, and anyone read as a woman by the system, wait longer for a diagnosis and get their pain dismissed as hormonal more often. That's not an accident of medicine. It's a documented pattern.

title: Rare Beyond Diagnosis: A Different Perspective on Rare Disease Day
description: Access to treatment gets all the attention on Rare Disease Day. The loneliness and disbelief patients face daily gets almost none of it, and it isn't unique to rare disease.

title: The Forgotten Price of Chronic Illness: A Systemic Approach to Reclaiming Wellness
description: Years spent chasing survival, appointment to appointment, taught me how to manage symptoms and made me forget how to actually live. Neglecting wellness has a cost too, even for people who are barely surviving.

title: Beyond the Buzzword: Why Patients Should Be the Pulse of Healthcare Innovation
description: Slapping 'patient-centric' on a product doesn't make it one. Patients aren't a data point to analyze. They're the people who should be in the room while the thing is actually being built.

title: Reclaiming Empathy in Healthcare
description: I used to see doctors as the people with the answers. Then I ended up on the other side of the exam table for years, and the empathy I'd assumed was standard turned out to be the exception.

title: How \\"Illness Porn\\" Changed Chronic Illness Forever
description: More chronically ill people are sharing stoma bags and feeding tubes on social media without apology. It made me uncomfortable at first. I've come to think that discomfort was the actual problem.

title: The Invisible Burden of Chronic Illness Loneliness
description: At 25, bedridden for three years with an illness nobody could name, I forgot what health even felt like. Loneliness isn't a side effect of chronic illness. It's part of the disease itself.

title: The Day Mental Health Is As Accessible As General Practice
description: What it would actually take for mental healthcare to work the way general practice does: same-day access, integrated records, no stigma, care where people already are.

title: The Coming Healthcare Revolution
description: On the Rabbit R1 and what AI-native hardware could mean for chronic disease management, clinician admin time, and access in regions without specialists, if the design includes patients from the start.

title: Fighting for certainty: Why Patients are seeking information outside of the doctor's office.
description: Doctors call it cyberchondria when patients research their own symptoms. It's not distrust. It's a response to feeling shut out of a process that's happening to your own body.

title: Patient Empowerment: A Year in Review and a Call to Action
description: 2023 had real progress on patient empowerment. Most of it was still cosmetic. A year-end accounting of what actually changed and what's still theater.

title: Is it time to finally empower Patients?
description: Care still mostly happens to patients, not with them. What empowerment actually requires, and why the system resists giving it up.

title: We are not clients.
description: Patients aren't clients. We don't come to you shopping for the best deal. We come vulnerable, looking for expertise, yes, but also empathy, and that distinction should shape how care actually gets delivered.

title: Embracing True Patient Centricity in Healthcare
description: Patient-centricity has become a popular word in healthcare marketing. What it would actually mean if organizations built decisions around it instead of just talking about it.

title: Valuing Patient Time as Much as Clinician Time
description: Patients wait weeks for an appointment, hours in the waiting room, and get minutes with the doctor. Healthcare treats clinician time as scarce and patient time as free.

title: Why disabled & chronically ill people are your best employees
description: I built eight organisations from my bed.

title: The Urge to Prove Our Worth
description: My doctor gave me a sticker that says 'slow' to put on my phone. I need the reminder, because every time illness loosens its grip, I try to make up for all the lost time at once.

title: Chronically Ignored
description: When I push too hard and end up bedridden for days, I get accused of faking it. Doctors have told me my nerve pain was 'all in my head' because a test didn't show it. This is what dismissal actually looks like.

title: The Invisible Struggle: The Mental Health Toll of Chronic Illness
description: My POTS self-diagnosis in my late twenties changed everything overnight. What almost nobody talks about is what it does to the mind, not just the body.

title: The Time is Now to Bring Mental Health into the Mainstream
description: Mental healthcare should be as easy to access as calling a doctor for the flu. It still requires fighting insurance loopholes, provider shortages, and a stigma that keeps people in the shadows.

title: Learning from Israel's Response to Collective Trauma
description: The scale of trauma after October's attacks is straining Israel's mental health system past what it was built for. What the response looks like, and why it has to be more than medical.

title: A Revolution in Medical Education: The Power of Partnership and Resilience
description: I taught a course at IMC Krems on patient narrative, provider resilience, and partnership. Notes on why medical education still trains for encounters, not relationships.

title: The Wounds That Do Not Heal: The Trauma of War on the Soul of a Nation
description: Written in the days after October 7th. Physical wounds mend. The trauma underneath them, in children, in veterans, in everyone who lived through it, needs a place to go too.

title: Ableism is everywhere.
description: A yoga instructor refused to modify poses for my chronic pain. A train conductor demanded I stand up despite a dizzy spell. Ableism isn't rare. It's structural, and it's mostly invisible to the people not experiencing it.

title: Your next speaker should be a patient.
description: Business leaders constantly seek fresh perspectives and insights to share with our teams and customers. The conventional route is to invite renowned academics, CEOs, and success...

title: Unlocking the Superpowers of Necessity: Why Chronically Ill and Disabled People May Be Our Best Employees
description: As an entrepreneur living with chronic pain, I've watched limitation get mistaken for weakness. It's usually the opposite: constraint is what built the skills employers actually need.

title: It's Time to Acknowledge Invisible Illness and Disability
description: I see the judging look every time I ask for help on a train or in an airport, because I don't look disabled. Society isn't trained to extend compassion to something it can't see.

title: It's Time for a Chief Patient Officer in Every Healthcare Organization
description: Healthcare organizations exist to serve patients, and patient advocacy is still usually an afterthought. Every one of them needs a Chief Patient Officer or a Patient in Residence.

title: It's Time to Lift the Taboo Off Mental Health
description: I've never met a chronically ill patient with no emotional involvement in their illness. That means I have a mental illness too. I'm done treating that as something to hide.

title: Is it Our Job to State Our Disabilities?
description: Imagine everyone carries an invisible backpack. Some carry a kilo, some ten. You can't tell by looking. That's what life with invisible illness is like, and it raises a real question: whose job is it to name it?

title: Patients are experts too.
description: Written after a lot of frustration being a patient keynote speaker. We are experts too. Pay us, treat us, and put us in decision-making positions like one.

title: The Isolated Archipelago of Illness
description: Every chronic illness is its own island. Diagnoses that look similar from the outside require completely different navigation once you're actually living on one.

title: Harnessing the Power of Patient Experience Data, Patient-Reported Outcomes, and Patient Empowerment in Chronic Illness Management
description: Three terms that get used interchangeably in chronic illness management, and why the difference between them actually matters.

title: Health Literacy: The First Step to Empowered Self-Management
description: Health literacy gets treated as a patient's reading-and-numeracy problem to fix. It's mostly a systems problem: confusing communication, opaque processes, and power imbalances.

title: Introducing Patient Schools: Empowering Chronic Patients through Education
description: I built Patient School because there was nowhere for chronically ill people to actually learn to manage their own condition, taught partly by patients who'd already done it.

title: The Importance of Having Your Own Resiliency Toolkit
description: I recently taught storytelling and resiliency to another cohort of Austria's Global Incubator Network. What actually goes into a resiliency toolkit, and why generic advice about it usually fails.

title: Empathy, Resilience, and Patient Empowerment in Medical School
description: For my master's thesis, I interviewed patients with chronic conditions alongside medical students and doctors. The pattern that came back from the patient side was consistent: they don't feel heard.

title: Empathy Training: A Promising Intervention for Improving Empathy Skills
description: A UC Berkeley study found empathy training actually works. Plus a book recommendation on what empathy is for.

title: Uplifting the Human Side of Healthcare
description: As a speaker with chronic illness, I'm both the performer and the audience every day. Plus: what the research says about PAs, NPs, and empathy in medicine.

title: Patient Empowerment: The Power of Post-Traumatic Growth
description: A study on post-traumatic growth found something worth passing on: doctors who grew from the pandemic were less likely to burn out, not more.

title: Empowering Change: Empathy, Equity, and Resilience in the Face of Chronic Illness
description: Three short notes: empathy as a medical skill, the barriers chronically ill speakers face on stage, and burnout in entrepreneurs.

title: Empowerment, Resilience, and Advocacy: Transforming Patient Experiences Worldwide
description: A hospital in Vienna left me bleeding on purpose, called it educational, and told me I was a burden. Also: notes from the Global Patient Participation Summit.

title: Paternalism to Empowerment
description: Medicine used to happen to patients. It's supposed to happen with them now. A hospital in Vienna reminded me how far that shift still has to go.

title: Issue 3: Revolutionizing Healthcare through Empathy, Innovation, and Patient Involvement
description: On medical gaslighting, a line from my own book, and what wearables actually change about patient outcomes.

title: Empowering Voices: Navigating Compassion, Advocacy, and the Patient Experience
description: I have POTS and post-viral syndrome myself, so a Washington Post piece on Long COVID and dysautonomia landed differently. Also: a KevinMD story on what one held hand can do.

title: Chronicles of Resilience: Empowering Voices in Chronic Illness
description: A short newsletter note: what happens when a hospital discharges a patient with nowhere to go, and why patients belong on the conference stage, not just in the audience.

title: How to manage expectations as a Chronically ill patient? (and how to support them as an HCP)
description: On the last episode of Revolution from Your Bed, season 3: managing expectations between patients, caregivers, and the healthcare professionals treating them.

title: Falling from Grace: Rising Beyond Relapse as an International Public Speaker with Chronic Illness
description: I built a career on the story of having survived something. Then I relapsed mid-career, in front of the same audiences, and had to figure out what my message was worth if I wasn't fixed after all.

title: Public speaker? Here are hard-learned lessons from Covid-19
description: I've made my living from keynotes, talks, and workshops for four years. When the pandemic hit, most speakers weren't ready for their whole business to move online overnight. Here's what I learned patching through it.

title: Prescription to a revolution or how to create a Patient-Led healthcare
description: I always wanted to be a doctor. Instead I became a patient for a decade, taught myself the diagnosis medicine had missed, and decided healthcare needed fixing more than I needed a medical degree.

title: How to start a revolution from your bed
description: I was recently honored to speak at TEDx Shanghai. My doctors gave me three big no's: I would never go to university, never work, never get married. I've done all three.
